item.title: FAA meets with airlines on plan to cut O'Hare flights
item.description: The FAA is considering reducing the number of flights at O'Hare Airport due to staffing shortages, tech trouble, and construction, which could lead to fewer flight options and higher airfares for travelers.

item.description: NEW YORK (AP/WGN) — A landmark new WNBA collective bargaining agreement was reached in principle early Wednesday morning that will give the league its first million-dollar players. item.title: '19 Kids and Counting' star charged with molestation and abuse during vacation
item.description: Joseph Garrett Duggar, star of TLC's "19 Kids and Counting", was arrested Wednesday for allegedly sexually abusing a minor during a family vacation in Panama City Beach.

item.title: Why Apple wants you to update your iPhone, iPad now
item.description: If you haven't updated your Apple device in a while, now may be the time to do it.

item.title: Illinois lawmakers plan to rescind Cesar Chavez Day
item.description: Illinois lawmakers are planning to rescind Cesar Chavez Day on March 31 and instead honor Dolores Huerta on her birthday, April 10, following allegations of sexual abuse by Chavez.

item.title: Suburban English teacher bring creativity, energy and empathy to the classroom
item.description: Matt Sniadecki, a teacher at Naperville North High School, was nominated by one of his students for his inspiring teaching style, empathy, and dedication to helping others, and was awarded $1,000 by Ankin Law.

item.title: 73-year-old Woodridge man faces felony charges after Tri-State Tollway police chase
Joliet City Council passes 795-acre AI data center development project
item.description: The Joliet City Council is set to decide the fate of a proposed 795-acre A.I. data center, which would use up to 150,000 gallons of water per day and 1.8 gigawatts of electricity, despite concerns from residents about the environmental impact and the city's water supply.
